messages.subject: (Another) Error in exists(name, envir = env, mode = mode)
parts:
The following code throws up this error.
difficulty <- ggplot(bothIsceds, aes(x=Difficulty,y = ..density..))+xlim(-4,3.5)
difficulty + geom_histogram( binwidth=.25, fill="steelblue") +   facet_grid(Isced ~ .)
difficulty + geom_vline(aes(xintercept = value), data = goodsetM )

It's the geom_vline which produces the error, though it looks just like p 86 of the ggplot2 book

I've read the other references to this error but they don't seem to refer to this case - it's not an empty dataset, not geom_area related and the numbers aren't strings.  The dataset is a data.frame:

str(goodsetM)
data.frame': 4 obs. of  2 variables:
 $ variable: Factor w/ 4 levels "A1","A2","B1",..: 1 2 3 4
 $ value   : num  -0.749 0.459 0.923 1.533

Very grateful for a solution.
Neil

messages.subject: Re: (Another) Error in exists(name, envir = env, mode = mode)
parts:
Hi:

This is not a reproducible example, but I can make a wild guess: in
your last line of code, you added geom_vline() to the **initial**
object difficulty, which did not contain a plot layer, hence did not
contain faceting information. You needed either to save the result of
the second line of code back to difficulty, or add both layers in one
call, as in

This should work.

-------

For future reference, let me introduce you to the concept of a working
reproducible example (WRE). This one contains fake data, but there are
many built-in data sets one can use to produce a WRE when appropriate.
It is designed to more or less replicate the intent of your graph.

# When generating random data, provide a random seed for reproducibility
set.seed(5290)

# Generate a data frame
DF <- data.frame(grp = rep(LETTERS[1:4], each = 100),
y = rnorm(400, mean = rep(c(0, 1, 2, 4), each = 100)))

# Get groupwise means
library(plyr)
xints <- ddply(DF, .(grp), summarise, mean = mean(y))

# Generate the graph
library(ggplot2)

ggplot(DF, aes(x = y, y = ..density..)) +
geom_histogram(fill = "steelblue", binwidth = 0.5) +
geom_vline(data = xints, aes(xintercept = mean)) +
facet_wrap(~ grp, ncol = 2)

One learns after a while that repeatedly saving a plot object after
each new layer is computed is not really necessary. It's in the book
because it is a useful way to teach what happens in each step of
creating a ggplot.
